query: For refractory materials, experiments at the solid-to-fluid transition are difficult and yield sparse, scattered data, while the large compositional space of high-entropy systems makes systematic screening impractical. DFT free-energy studies can determine the transition from the crossing of solid and dense-fluid Gibbs energies and provide associated thermodynamic properties, but their reliance on extensive ab initio molecular dynamics makes them costly. TOR-TILD has shown high efficiency for elemental and binary systems, yet becomes substantially slower for multicomponent systems. Any broadly useful approach must retain ab initio-level accuracy, represent all thermodynamic effects identified as important, treat both phases around the transition, and remain practical across relevant compositions and temperatures. For a multicomponent high-entropy material in these high-temperature states, what single intervention could improve determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and causal mechanism, its predicted outcome relative to existing experimental and computational baselines, its boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive experiment or benchmark that would falsify it.

cited_evidence.text: A concept for accelerated assessment of MPEAs has recently been proposed. Here we develop and apply this idea to quickly identify, screen and analyze structural alloys for use at moderate and high temperatures. We select a palette of 26 metallic elements that are most likely to produce the moderate and high-temperature properties ranges in MPEAs. The palette of elements is shown in Supplementary Table 1. Phase diagrams are the road maps for materials design, and give essential information on the phases present at a given alloy chemistry and temperature. Most binary and some ternary phase diagrams have been determined experimentally, but multi-component systems remain largely unexplored. Experimental measurement of multi-component phase diagrams is impractical due to the tremendous amount of work involved. In recent years, integration of the CALPHAD approach with key experiments has been demonstrated as an effective approach to determine complicated multi-component phase diagrams. The essence of the CALPHAD approach is to use experimental data from constituent binary and ternary phase diagrams to develop a thermodynamic database. High entropy alloys (HEAs), which contain multiple principal elements, have recently attracted considerable research interest due to their exceptional mechanical and physical properties, such as high corrosion, wear, fatigue resistances, yield strength, ductility, and thermal stability,, often outperforming traditional alloys and super-alloys, especially at low and high temperatures,. However, the design (compositional and chemical) space of HEAs is vast, which makes the use of the conventional methods based on lengthy, costly, high-fidelity (HF) approaches, a daunting task. An efficient strategy is thus highly demanded to screen and design HEAs with optimal mechanical and physical properties for specific applications,. Machine learning (ML) is emerging as a powerful tool for inductive screening and phase selection of HEAs. However, the accuracy of ML is strongly dependent on the size and quality of used dataset . The lack of a large-size, high-quality dataset for HEAs is currently a major challenge for using ML.
